problem: Embodied AI research is fragmented across simulators (AI2-THOR, Habitat, CARLA, …), tasks and codebases. Moving a model trained in one environment to another, swapping PPO for A2C, adding an IL warm-start, or adding an auxiliary loss requires large code changes. Gym-style Env abstractions tie the goal to the environment, which fits poorly with embodied settings where one simulator hosts many tasks. As a result, most papers evaluate on a single task, environment and modality.
motivation: The authors annotated the 20+ most-cited Embodied AI papers (via S2ORC). Most evaluate only one task, environment and modality, and there is little standardization of algorithms. This signals high barriers to replication, to ablations, to ramping up new researchers, and to reusing expensive trained models. The authors observe that code changes follow a frequency pattern (hyperparameters daily-weekly; architectures and pipelines weekly-monthly; new environments, tasks and losses quarterly-yearly), and they want a framework whose abstractions make each of these changes cheap.
key_idea: A modular PyTorch framework for Embodied AI that decouples Task from Environment, generates episodes through a TaskSampler, defines experiments in code, and makes multi-stage and multi-loss training pipelines (IL→RL, DAgger, auxiliary losses, DD-PPO/A2C) first-class. It ships reproduced baselines and pre-trained models across iTHOR, RoboTHOR, Habitat and MiniGrid.
insight: The main lessons are about software abstractions, not a new model. Separating Task (actions, rewards, success) from Environment (state manipulation), and replacing Gym's self-resetting env with a TaskSampler (curricula, controlled goal streams), confines most changes to one class. Making TrainingPipeline stages a core object lets an IL warm-start be added with one line. The reproduction experiments support three points: (i) DD-PPO at 75M frames reproduces the Habitat PointNav baseline (92.5% validation), and a ResNet+LSTM ObjectNav model beats the best CVPR'20 RoboTHOR challenge entry; (ii) on BabyAI GoToLocal, IL variants converge far faster than RL, and A2C is markedly less sample-efficient than PPO; (iii) on MiniGrid LC Corrupt S15N7, IL→PPO sequences rescue the near-zero performance of IL or RL alone, while ADVISOR's adaptive parallel IL+RL combination performs best (10 seeds, 50-sample hyperparameter search per baseline).
method: ExperimentConfig: experiments are defined as Python classes rather than text configs, so new hyperparameters and architectures are easy to add and IDE type hints and auto-completion work.

Task/Environment decoupling: the Environment only exposes state manipulation; the Task defines the action space, rewards and success criteria and mediates between agent and environment, so one simulator (e.g. AI2-THOR) can host many tasks.
TaskSampler: replaces Gym's reset and gives full control over the sequence of task instances, e.g. curriculum learning by sampling progressively harder instances (generalizes Habitat-API's Dataset).

TrainingPipeline of PipelineStages: each stage specifies its losses, training length or early stopping, and a teacher-forcing schedule. This enables sequential IL→RL and simultaneous multi-loss training such as PPO plus a self-supervised loss, or ADVISOR.

Algorithms: decentralized distributed synchronous on-policy training (built on DD-PPO from Habitat-API) with A2C, PPO, IL, or arbitrary user losses (e.g. DD-A2C, DD-curiosity). Off-policy relaxations are teacher forcing (DAgger via a linear-decay expert probability) and training on fixed external demonstration datasets, interleaved with on-policy updates.

Multi-agent support, Tensorboard visualization plug-ins (egocentric, top-down and third-person views, per-step policy distributions), tutorials, type hints, and pre-trained checkpoints for the reproduced baselines.

setting.backbone: Task-dependent policies trained from scratch in the framework: DD-PPO agents for PointNav; ResNet + LSTM for ObjectNav; the BabyAI model of Chevalier-Boisvert et al. for GoToLocal; embedding + GRU (512) actor-critic for Stag Hunt; the original ALFRED pre-trained model for the ALFRED re-implementation
setting.training_data: Simulator training episodes only: PointNav trained 75M frames; ObjectNav (iTHOR/RoboTHOR) 200M steps with DD-PPO; BabyAI GoToLocal with PPO, A2C, BC, DAgger, BC^tf=1, and BC^off-policy on a fixed 1M expert-demonstration dataset; MiniGrid LC Corrupt with IL→RL and ADVISOR; Stag Hunt 3M steps (~66.7K episodes)
setting.observation: Egocentric visual observations; the paper does not specify RGB vs. depth for the navigation experiments. PointNav additionally gets the goal displacement vector and ObjectNav a category label. Grid worlds use a 7×7 egocentric view (BabyAI, with a 5-word instruction) or the full map (Stag Hunt).
setting.action_space: Discrete low-level: MoveAhead 0.25 m, turn 30° (plus stop) for navigation; discrete grid moves in MiniGrid/BabyAI/MultiGrid
setting.privileged: none beyond the task-defined goal specification (PointNav goal displacement vector)

numbers.extra: Trained 75M frames. The paper only says 'Habitat' (the dataset is likely Gibson, given the comparison to Habitat/DD-PPO baselines); sensor modality is unspecified. 'Validation accuracy' is presumably success rate. Success = stop within 0.2 m.
numbers.evidence: Sec. 4: 'We train DD-PPO for 75 million frames and obtain a validation accuracy of 92.5%.'

numbers.extra: Test-seen split. Reproduction of the original ALFRED baseline inside AllenAct, not a new method. GC = goal-condition success rate.
numbers.evidence: Sec. 4: 'using their pre-trained model, we obtain a 4.0% task success rate and 9.4% on the goal condition success rate on the test-seen scenario.'

numbers.method: Multi-agent actor-critic (GRU) reproduction of Markov Stag Hunt
numbers.backbone: Embedding (8) + shared GRU (512) + per-agent linear actor-critic heads
numbers.extra: 5×5 MultiGrid map, 45 steps, trained 3M steps; evaluated on 1000 trajectories × 5 seeds. Reward reported as mean ± std for penalty g=0.5 and g=3.0.
numbers.evidence: Sec. 4: 'Our reproduced model achieves 124.7±2.47, and 57.0±4.21 reward as g={0.5, 3.0} at 3M training steps'

numbers_note: The iTHOR/RoboTHOR PointNav and ObjectNav results (SR, SPL), the BabyAI GoToLocal curves and the MiniGrid LC Corrupt S15N7 comparisons appear only in figures (Fig. 3a–c, Stag Hunt in an appendix figure), with no numeric values in the text. The text only states that the RoboTHOR ObjectNav model outperforms the best CVPR'20 RoboTHOR challenge entry. The Habitat PointNav dataset and sensors are not stated explicitly.
results: AllenAct reproduces known results across several environments. DD-PPO PointNav in Habitat reaches 92.5% validation accuracy at 75M frames, slightly above the Habitat (Savva et al. 2019) baseline trained for the same budget. A ResNet+LSTM ObjectNav agent trained 200M steps beats the best CVPR'20 RoboTHOR challenge submission. BabyAI/BabyAI-style IL and RL findings are reproduced (IL converges faster; A2C is less sample-efficient than PPO), as are the ADVISOR findings (IL→RL helps; ADVISOR is best on LC Corrupt), Markov Stag Hunt equilibria (124.7 reward at g=0.5), and ALFRED test-seen numbers (4.0% SR, 9.4% GC).
limitations: This is a framework paper: there is no new navigation method, and most navigation results are shown only in plots with few exact numbers.

The early release supports only synchronous, on-policy training (plus teacher forcing and fixed-dataset IL). Deep Q-learning and asynchronous training are left for future work, and VLN, SAPIEN, ThreeDWorld and multi-agent furniture tasks are only planned.
PointNav training is limited to 75M frames, well below DD-PPO's 2.5B-frame state of the art; details such as sensors and dataset are sparse.
